title.en: Do not read distances off a nonlinear embedding

summary: Present nonlinear projections with their interpretation limits and let the viewer vary the parameters that change the picture.
objective: Keep an embedding scene from asserting similarity relationships the projection does not preserve.
applies_when: High-dimensional data is displayed through a non-linear neighbour embedding such as t-SNE, whose caveats below apply directly.
Clusters, gaps or distances in the projection are discussed.
The projection has parameters such as perplexity or a random seed.
Another dimensionality reduction is used, such as a linear projection, and its own interpretation rules must be stated instead of inheriting these.
intent_signals: why does the plot keep changing
example_prompts: Show the embedding projection with its interpretation caveats.
Let me change the projection parameters and see how the picture changes.
negative_signals: Linear projections such as principal components, where distance behaviour differs and can be stated exactly.
Data with genuine spatial coordinates, where position is not a projection artefact.
not_for: Linear projections such as principal components, where distance behaviour differs and can be stated exactly.
Data with genuine spatial coordinates, where position is not a projection artefact.

principles: The projection is a lossy transformation with its own dynamics. In t-SNE plots the relative sizes of clusters cannot be read, because the method expands dense clusters and contracts sparse ones, and the distances between well-separated clusters may mean nothing.

Parameters change the answer. Perplexity balances local against global structure, and there may be no single value that captures distances across all clusters, so a single plot is one view among many.
Because the layout is stochastic and parameter-dependent, a scene should make reruns and parameter changes available rather than presenting one run as the structure of the data.

Neighbourhood membership is not guaranteed by an embedding: check important similarity claims in the original space. Choose caveats by method. PCA can report component loadings and calculated explained variance; an arbitrary linear map has no automatic PCA variance-ordering interpretation.
implementation: State the method, its parameters and the random seed in the scene, and make reruns possible.
Provide parameter controls and show how the picture changes, which is the most direct way to convey the limitation.
Support checking a claim in the original space, for example by reporting original-space distances for selected points.

For a neighbour embedding, avoid implying that coordinate rulers measure original-space distance. For a linear projection, label the actual map or components; report explained variance only when that quantity has been defined and calculated for the chosen method, such as PCA.
Where a claim about similarity matters, verify it against the source data rather than the projection.
observable_checks: Rerun with a different seed and compare explicitly: report which features of the picture persist and which move. A stable result may look almost unchanged, which is informative rather than a failure, and a conclusion that does not survive reseeding must be surfaced as unstable rather than quietly retained.
Change the perplexity or equivalent parameter and observe how cluster spacing and size change.
Select two points that appear close and compare their distance in the original space.

Confirm each readout names its space and method. A neighbour-embedding ruler must not imply original-space distance; a linear projection should identify its map/components and show explained variance only when defined and computed, not merely because the map is linear.

creative_affordances: Embeddings remain excellent for exploration and for finding candidates to inspect; the rule restricts the claims, not the use.
Animated transitions between parameter settings can be an engaging way to teach the caveat.
known_limits: Authored guidance citing published interpretation caveats for one method; other projection methods have their own behaviours not covered here.
It does not evaluate any specific embedding implementation.

claims.statement: In t-SNE plots the relative sizes of clusters cannot be read because the method naturally expands dense clusters and contracts sparse ones, distances between well-separated clusters may mean nothing, and the perplexity parameter trades local against global structure so that different values produce substantially different pictures.
claims.scope: Interpretation limits of t-SNE embeddings; other dimensionality-reduction methods behave differently.

source_refs.locator: Cluster sizes mean nothing; distances between clusters might not mean anything; perplexity discussion
